     7	import React from 'react'
     8	import {FormattedMessage, FormattedNumber, useIntl} from 'react-intl'
     9	import {
    10	    Stack,
    11	    Text,
    12	    useBreakpointValue
    13	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui'
    14	import {useItemVariant} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/item-variant'
    15	import {getPriceData} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils'
    16	import DisplayPrice from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/display-price'
    17	import {ZimmProductPrice} from '../ui-kits/atoms/zimmProductPrice'
    18	
    19	type PricePerItemProps = {
    20	    currency: string
    21	    basePrice?: number
    22	}
    23	
    24	const PricePerItem = ({currency, basePrice}: PricePerItemProps) => {
    25	    return (
    26	        <Text fontSize={{base: '12px', lg: '14px'}}>
    27	            <FormattedNumber style="currency" currency={currency} value={basePrice ?? 0} />
    28	            <FormattedMessage
    29	                defaultMessage="ea"
    30	                id="price_per_item.label.each"
    31	                description="Abbreviated 'each', follows price per item, like $10/ea"
    32	            />
    33	        </Text>
    34	    )
    35	}
    36	
    37	type ItemPriceProps = {
    38	    currency: string
    39	    align?: string
    40	    baseDirection?: string
    41	    [key: string]: unknown
    42	}
    43	
    44	/**
    45	 * In the context of a cart product item variant, this component renders the item's
    46	 * pricing, taking into account applied discounts as well as base item prices.
    47	 * When an item-level promotion reduces the price, the original price is shown
    48	 * crossed out beside the discounted current price.
    49	 */
    50	const ItemPrice = ({currency, align = 'right', baseDirection = 'column', ...props}: ItemPriceProps) => {
    51	    const variant = useItemVariant() as Record<string, unknown>
    52	    const price = variant?.price as number | undefined
    53	    const priceAfterItemDiscount = variant?.priceAfterItemDiscount as number | undefined
    54	    const priceAfterOrderDiscount = variant?.priceAfterOrderDiscount as number | undefined
    55	    const isASet = (variant?.type as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.set as boolean | undefined
    56	    const isMaster = (variant?.type as Record<string, unknown> | undefined)?.master as boolean | undefined
    57	    const quantity = ((variant?.quantity as number | undefined) ?? 1)
    58	
    59	    // Use the most-discounted price as the displayed current price: after all order-level
    60	    // adjustments if available, otherwise after item-level adjustments.
    61	    const effectiveCurrentPrice = priceAfterOrderDiscount ?? priceAfterItemDiscount ?? price ?? 0
    62	    const isOnSale = (price ?? 0) > effectiveCurrentPrice
    63	
    64	    let priceData
    65	    if (variant?.itemId) {
    66	        priceData = {
    67	            currentPrice: effectiveCurrentPrice,
    68	            // Show the original price crossed out when any promotion (item- or order-level) has
    69	            // reduced the price. The base SFCC component sets listPrice: null to suppress this.
    70	            listPrice: isOnSale ? price : null,
    71	            // Divide effectiveCurrentPrice (after all discounts) by quantity rather than using
    72	            // variant.pricePerUnit, which SFCC computes from the original list price and would
    73	            // show the wrong per-unit value when an order-level discount is applied.
    74	            pricePerUnit: quantity > 0 ? effectiveCurrentPrice / quantity : effectiveCurrentPrice,
    75	            isASet,
    76	            isMaster,
    77	            isRange: isASet || isMaster || false,
    78	            isOnSale
    79	        }
    80	    } else {
    81	        priceData = getPriceData(variant)
    82	    }
    83	    const isDesktop = useBreakpointValue({base: false, lg: true})
    84	    const intl = useIntl()
    85	
    86	    return (
    87	        <Stack
    88	            textAlign={align}
    89	            direction={baseDirection}
    90	            justifyContent={align === 'left' ? 'flex-start' : 'flex-end'}
    91	            alignItems="baseline"
    92	            spacing={priceData?.isOnSale ? 0 : 1}
    93	            wrap="nowrap"
    94	            {...props}
    95	        >
    96	            {!isDesktop && quantity > 1 && !isASet && priceData?.pricePerUnit && (
    97	                <PricePerItem currency={currency} basePrice={priceData.pricePerUnit} />
    98	            )}
    99	
   100	            {variant?.itemId && isOnSale ? (
   101	                // ZimmProductPrice already owns the Was/Now label treatment — reuse it rather
   102	                // than duplicating the label strings and styling. Prices are formatted here
   103	                // because ZimmProductPrice expects pre-formatted strings, not raw numbers.
   104	                <ZimmProductPrice
   105	                    currentPrice={intl.formatNumber(effectiveCurrentPrice, {style: 'currency', currency})}
   106	                    originalPrice={intl.formatNumber(price ?? 0, {style: 'currency', currency})}
   107	                    isLive={true}
   108	                />
   109	            ) : variant?.itemId ? (
   110	                <DisplayPrice
   111	                    labelForA11y={variant?.name as string}
   112	                    currency={currency}
   113	                    priceData={priceData}
   114	                    listPriceProps={{fontSize: 'sm'}}
   115	                />
   116	            ) : (
   117	                <DisplayPrice
   118	                    labelForA11y={variant?.name as string}
   119	                    currency={currency}
   120	                    priceData={priceData}
   121	                    quantity={variant?.quantity as number}
   122	                    listPriceProps={{fontSize: 'sm'}}
   123	                />
   124	            )}
   125	
   126	            {isDesktop && quantity > 1 && !isASet && priceData?.pricePerUnit && (
   127	                <PricePerItem currency={currency} basePrice={priceData.pricePerUnit} />
   128	            )}
   129	        </Stack>
   130	    )
   131	}
   132	
   133	export default ItemPrice

    81	                select: '(data.(id,name,master.(masterId),type.(bundle,master,set),c_isSale,variationAttributes.(id,name,values.(value,name)),imageGroups[viewType=small].(viewType,images.(link,disBaseLink,alt),variationAttributes.(id,values.(value)))))'

     8	import OrderSummary from './index';

    11	// calls useCurrentBasket() -> useSFPayments() -> useAppOrigin() -> useOrigin() — the same chain
    12	// documented at header/index.stories.tsx, needing the identical provider stack for the same
    13	// reason: ServerContext has no default value, so the unconditional `{res}` destructure inside
    14	// useOrigin throws without a provider, regardless of environment. disableAuthInit means no real
    15	// SFCC auth call fires, and usePromoCode's own basket resolves to undefined here — harmless,
    16	// since this component's own basket data always comes from the `basket` prop below, not from
    17	// usePromoCode's internal fetch.
    18	const storybookQueryClient = new QueryClient({
    19	  defaultOptions: { queries: { retry: false, refetchOnWindowFocus: false } },
    20	});

- **What wraps `ItemName`?** `:66` a bare `<div>` containing `<h2>`.

- **`aria-describedby`?** None.
- **`role="group"`?** None.

```

  <span data-testid="product-now-price">Now $595.00</span>
```

Two further factual consequences of the swap, both verifiable in the cited lines:

1. The live region moves from a hidden sibling node onto the **visible** price node. With `isLive={true}` hard-coded at PR `item-price.tsx:107`, every discounted line in a cart mounts its own `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` region. `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:56-62` documents `isLive={false}` as the intended setting for exactly this case ("a grid of many cards … where the price never changes after mount"), and `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:157` + its test at `index.test.tsx:181` show that precedent being applied.

That premise holds on the PDP (single price, focus stays put). It does not hold in a cart of N lines, where the name prefix was the disambiguator.

`overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-price.test.tsx` (PR branch) contains **no** a11y assertions — grepped for `aria|VisuallyHidden|labelForA11y|current price|original price`; the only `name` hits are the `baseVariant` fixture at `:68` and a doc line at `:7`.

# PDP colour/size selection navigation — findings

## Mechanism note (affects how to read all of this)

`package.json:17-20` sets `ccExtensibility: {extends: "@salesforce/retail-react-app", overridesDir: "overrides"}`. Any file at `overrides/app/<path>` shadows `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/<path>`. Relevant consequences:

- `overrides/app/utils/url.ts` fully shadows the base `app/utils/url.js` and re-implements `productUrlBuilder`, `rebuildPathWithParams`, `updateSearchParams` itself (`overrides/app/utils/url.ts:60`, `:73`, `:199`).
- `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/recommended-products/index.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/item-variant/*` all shadow their base counterparts.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller/index.jsx` is **not** shadowed, and still renders base `ProductTile`.

---

# QUESTION 1 — `?color=` presence on inbound PDP links

## The two URL builders

- `overrides/app/utils/url.ts:199` — `export const productUrlBuilder = (product: { id: string }): string => encodeURI(`/product/${product.id}`);` → **bare path, no query params at all.**
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url.js:98` — identical bare path.
- `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url.js:35-46` / `overrides/app/utils/url.ts:60` — `rebuildPathWithParams` is the only thing that adds params, and only if a caller passes them. `updateSearchParams` (`url.js:48-57`) **deletes** a key when its value is falsy, so a `rebuildPathWithParams(url, {color: undefined})` produces **no** `color=`.

## Link sources that DO NOT carry `?color=`

| Source | file:line | href produced |
|---|---|---|
| **PLP product grid** | `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts:290` — `href: buildUrl(productUrlBuilder({ id: hit.productId }))` | `/<site>/<locale>/product/<id>` — no query string. Note `productListCardMapper.ts:286` resolves a *representative colour* for the card's images (`resolveRepresentativeColour(hit)`) but that colour is **never** put in the href. |
| PLP card wrapper | `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx:745` → `:806` `<ProductListCard {...}/>` → `:229-231` spreads `cardProps` straight into `ZimmProductCard`; href untouched | unchanged |

| **Recently-viewed rail** (PDP/Cart/PLP) | `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedCard.ts:225` — `href: buildUrl(productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id }))` | no query string |
| **Recently-viewed full-history page** | `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts:404` — same expression | no query string |
| **Cart / checkout / confirmation / order-detail / wishlist / order-summary / multiship line items** | `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-image.tsx:105` `<Link to={`/product/${productId}`}>` and `overrides/app/components/item-variant/item-name.tsx:78` `to={`/product/${productId}`}`; `productId` = `variant?.master?.masterId \|\| variant.id` (`item-image.tsx:95`, `item-name.tsx:74`) | **master** id, no `color=`, no `pid=` — the specific purchased colour is discarded |

# QUESTION 2 — how `urlColour` is derived

**`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:324`:**

```ts
const urlColour = new URLSearchParams(location.search).get(SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID) ?? undefined;
```

- `location` is `useLocation()` (`:131`, `:223`).
- `SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID` is `'color'` (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:164`).
- The expression is **purely the URL read**. There is **no** fallback to a default or first-offered colour in the value of `urlColour` itself.

Two separate, distinct fallbacks exist elsewhere:

1. **Display-only fallback at the render site** — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1263`: `selectedValue={urlColour ?? attr.selectedValue?.value}`. Plus `ZimmColourSwatchGroup`'s own internal fallback: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:96` — `const effectiveSelectedValue = offered.some((v) => v.value === selectedValue) ? selectedValue : offered[0]?.value;`. Neither changes `urlColour`.

2. **A URL-writing effect that makes `urlColour` non-falsy shortly after mount** — `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:413-431`:
```ts
useEffect(() => {
  if (urlColour) return;
  if (product?.id !== requestedProductId) return;
  const colourAttr = product?.variationAttributes?.find((a) => a.id === SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
  const defaultColourValue = (colourAttr?.values as SfccSwatchAttrValue[] | undefined)?.find(
    (v) => v.orderable !== false,
  )?.value;
  if (!defaultColourValue) return;
  const params = new URLSearchParams(location.search);
  params.set(SFCC_COLOUR_ATTRIBUTE_ID, defaultColourValue);
  history.replace(`${location.pathname}?${params.toString()}`);
}, [urlColour, product, requestedProductId]);
```
So on a `?color=`-less arrival, `urlColour` is `undefined` for the first render(s) — until `product.id === requestedProductId` and a first orderable colour value exists — then a `history.replace` writes `?color=<first orderable>` and `urlColour` becomes truthy on the next render. It stays `undefined` forever if `defaultColourValue` is falsy (`:427`).

Also consumed at `:459` and `:464` by `selectVariantScopedPriceData` (`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/variantScopedPrice.ts:92`, `:113-117`).

# QUESTION 4 — does changing colour remount `ProductView`?

## No `key` on `<ProductView>`

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1212-1318` — the standard-product `<ProductView ... />`. Its full prop list (read at `1212-1318`) contains **no `key=` prop**. The set/bundle parent instance at `:1118` likewise has none; the per-child instance at `:1144` is keyed on the enclosing `<Box key={childProduct.id}>` (`:1143`) — a product id, not the colour.

`ProductView` is a module-level `forwardRef` (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:379`, `:1683`, exported at `:1692`) — stable element type across renders, and not wrapped in `React.memo`.

The only `key`s in the PDP render path that move on navigation are:

- `:1094` — `key={id}` on `<meta>` tags.

`<Island hydrateOn={'visible'}>` (`:1211`) is a pass-through wrapper (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/island/index.jsx:86-90`) and adds no key.

## Route behaviour on a query-string-only change

`overrides/app/routes.tsx:75-78`:
```ts
{
  path: '/product/:productId',
  component: ProductDetail,
},
```
react-router v5 matches on `pathname` only; `location.search` is not part of the path match. A colour swatch `history.push` changes only the search string, so the same `<Route>` stays matched with the same `component` reference (`ProductDetail`, a `loadable` created once at module scope) — **the route does not unmount**. The component re-renders with a new `location` object.

Supporting evidence that the codebase relies on exactly this: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:284-297` sets `keepPreviousData: true` on `useProduct` with an explicit comment that `ZimmProductContent` "never unmounts on a variant change, so the price element survives and React mutates its text in place" for the `aria-live` announcement. A remount would defeat that.

## Conclusion

On a colour query-param change the `ProductView` subtree is **re-rendered, not remounted**. Nothing in the render path changes the React element identity or key of `<ProductView>` when `?color=` changes — no `key`, no conditional element type, no wrapper keyed on location, and no route unmount.

So a previously selected size stays selected across a colour swap, and `effectiveControlledVariationValues` (`:471-483`) stays non-null, which in turn keeps `useVariationAttributes` in controlled mode and keeps `v.href === null` for the gallery-overlay swatches (see Q3c).

## No `key` on `<ProductView>`

`<Island hydrateOn={'visible'}>` (`:1211`) is a pass-through wrapper (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/island/index.jsx:86-90`) and adds no key.

## Route behaviour on a query-string-only change

`overrides/app/routes.tsx:75-78`:
```ts
{
  path: '/product/:productId',
  component: ProductDetail,
},
```
react-router v5 matches on `pathname` only; `location.search` is not part of the path match. A colour swatch `history.push` changes only the search string, so the same `<Route>` stays matched with the same `component` reference (`ProductDetail`, a `loadable` created once at module scope) — **the route does not unmount**. The component re-renders with a new `location` object.

Supporting evidence that the codebase relies on exactly this: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:284-297` sets `keepPreviousData: true` on `useProduct` with an explicit comment that `ZimmProductContent` "never unmounts on a variant change, so the price element survives and React mutates its text in place" for the `aria-live` announcement. A remount would defeat that.

On a colour query-param change the `ProductView` subtree is **re-rendered, not remounted**. Nothing in the render path changes the React element identity or key of `<ProductView>` when `?color=` changes — no `key`, no conditional element type, no wrapper keyed on location, and no route unmount.


# QUESTION 4 — does changing colour remount `ProductView`?

## No `key` on `<ProductView>`

`overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1212-1318` — the standard-product `<ProductView ... />`. Its full prop list (read at `1212-1318`) contains **no `key=` prop**. The set/bundle parent instance at `:1118` likewise has none; the per-child instance at `:1144` is keyed on the enclosing `<Box key={childProduct.id}>` (`:1143`) — a product id, not the colour.

`ProductView` is a module-level `forwardRef` (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:379`, `:1683`, exported at `:1692`) — stable element type across renders, and not wrapped in `React.memo`.

The only `key`s in the PDP render path that move on navigation are:
- `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:1381` — `key={location.key}` on the **"Recently Viewed" `RecommendedProducts`** rail only (comment at `:1379-1380`). This *does* remount on every colour click, but it is a sibling of `ProductView`, not an ancestor.
- `:1321` — `key={activePdpTabId ?? 'closed'}` on `ZimmPdpDrawer`.
- `:1094` — `key={id}` on `<meta>` tags.

`<Island hydrateOn={'visible'}>` (`:1211`) is a pass-through wrapper (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/island/index.jsx:86-90`) and adds no key.

## Route behaviour on a query-string-only change

`overrides/app/routes.tsx:75-78`:
```ts
{
  path: '/product/:productId',
  component: ProductDetail,
},
```
react-router v5 matches on `pathname` only; `location.search` is not part of the path match. A colour swatch `history.push` changes only the search string, so the same `<Route>` stays matched with the same `component` reference (`ProductDetail`, a `loadable` created once at module scope) — **the route does not unmount**. The component re-renders with a new `location` object.

Supporting evidence that the codebase relies on exactly this: `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx:284-297` sets `keepPreviousData: true` on `useProduct` with an explicit comment that `ZimmProductContent` "never unmounts on a variant change, so the price element survives and React mutates its text in place" for the `aria-live` announcement. A remount would defeat that.

## Conclusion

On a colour query-param change the `ProductView` subtree is **re-rendered, not remounted**. Nothing in the render path changes the React element identity or key of `<ProductView>` when `?color=` changes — no `key`, no conditional element type, no wrapper keyed on location, and no route unmount.

**Direct behavioural consequence worth noting:** because `ProductView` is not remounted, its `localSizeValue` state (`overrides/app/components/product-view/index.tsx:469`) survives a colour change. `setLocalSizeValue` is called at exactly one place — `:1290`, the size selector's `onSelectionChange` — and there is no reset effect (the only location/variation-keyed effect in the file is `:1017-1021`, which merely calls `toggleShowOptionsMessage(false)`). So a previously selected size stays selected across a colour swap, and `effectiveControlledVariationValues` (`:471-483`) stays non-null, which in turn keeps `useVariationAttributes` in controlled mode and keeps `v.href === null` for the gallery-overlay swatches (see Q3c).

I've settled everything from source. Cleaning up: the temp worktree is removed and the working tree is untouched (only your own pre-existing `zimmCartItemActions`/`zimmQuantityStepper`/`cartDrawerContainer` edits remain). ## Gates I re-ran myself (detached worktree at `1a32bc94`, `node_modules` symlinked) | Gate | Result | |---|---| | `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean (exit 0) — confirms yours | | `vitest` on the 2 new test files | 15 tests, all pass — confirms your +15 | | `eslint` on the 5 new/changed files | **518 problems: 516 `prettier/prettier`, 1 `no-non-null-assertion` (error), 1 unused-eslint-disable (warn)** — accounts for 518 of your +524 | | `node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs` | 11 unacknowledged; **exactly 5 are the new files** — accounts for your 6→11 | --- ## A. The a11y regression — confirmed, but not in the direction the brief assumes **What `labelForA11y` actually produces.** `display-price/current-price.jsx:56-66` renders a second, hidden node: `{labelForA11y}{"current price $X"}`. `list-price.jsx:55-61` does the same with `"original price $Y"` (`messages.js:17-28`). Its own inline comment states the purpose: *"we want to make sure the product name is announced before the price to avoid confusion."* The visible ``/`` additionally carry `aria-label="current price $X"` / `"original price $Y"` (`current-price.jsx:49-51`, `list-price.jsx:47-49`). **Before vs after, for a discounted cart line:** - **Base** (`item-price.jsx:51-56`) sets `listPrice: null` *unconditionally* — so base never showed a strikethrough in the cart at all. A screen reader heard: `"current price $595.00"` then `"Silk Midi Dresscurrent price $595.00"` (name and label concatenated with no separator — a base wart). - **Head** (`item-price.tsx:100-108`) renders `

Was $795.00 Now $595.00

`. Heard: **`"Was $795.00 Now $595.00"`** — no product name, no `current price`/`original price` role words. So it is **better in one respect** (the original price is now announced at all) and **worse in two** (name gone, semantic price labels gone). That changes the fix from "revert" to "add the name back". **Is the name associated any other way? No — search scope stated.** I had an agent grep for `aria-labelledby|aria-describedby|role="group"|NAME` with **no `id`**. The price sits three roleless `
`s over in a cousin subtree — no shared accessible-name scope exists. `ItemPrice` spreads `{...props}`, so a caller *could* inject `aria-labelledby`; I checked all 8 call sites and none passes any `aria-*`. **Blast radius is 8 surfaces, not just the cart** — every one imports the base specifier, so all receive the override: base `product-item/index.jsx:19` (cart page + wishlist), `order-summary/index.jsx:30`, `multiship/multiship-order-summary.jsx:22`, `pages/confirmation/index.jsx:47`, `checkout/partials/shipping-product-cards.jsx:18`, `checkout/partials/pickup-address.jsx:29`, `account/order-detail.jsx:34`, and the PR's own `overrides/app/components/order-summary/index.tsx:29`. --- ## B. Live regions — the count is unchanged; the content is what broke **Correction to the brief's premise, both halves:** 1. **All five `aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true"` in `order-summary/index.tsx` (lines 207, 229, 250, 316, 348) are inherited verbatim** from base `order-summary/index.jsx` (lines 160, 180, 194, 248, 280). Not new. Nothing to raise there. 2. **N discounted items do not add N *new* live regions.** Base `DisplayPrice` already put one `aria-live` region on *every* cart line via that `VisuallyHidden` node. So it's 1 region per line before and 1 after. What actually changed: the region **moved from a hidden sibling onto the visible price node** (`zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:94-96`, `:136`), and **lost its name prefix**. **Mechanism on a basket mutation.** An order-level promotion is distributed across all line items, so changing *one* line's quantity mutates `priceAfterOrderDiscount` on *every* line. Each discounted line's `

` text changes → `aria-atomic="true"` re-reads the whole thing → N polite announcements queue up as `"Was $795.00 Now $595.00"`, `"Was $450.00 Now $337.50"`, … with **nothing identifying which line each belongs to**, plus the 5 inherited summary rows if the summary is on screen. Base was equally noisy but each announcement was self-identifying. **The name prefix was the only disambiguator, and that is precisely what was dropped** — so the regression is in B, not just A. Two mechanism details worth having: removing an item unmounts its `ItemVariantProvider` (keyed `order-summary-item-{productId}-{itemId}`, line 126-128), and a *removed* or *newly inserted* live region announces nothing — so "remove item" announces only the surviving lines' discount redistribution. And base `product-item/index.jsx` renders `CartItemVariantPrice` **twice** (`:71` `HideOnDesktop`, `:104` `HideOnMobile`); `responsive/index.jsx:16-34` hides via `display: none`, which removes from the a11y tree — so one active region per line, not two. --- ## C. Type scale — the concern is real but *inverted*; the i18n concern is real as stated **Actual resolved values.** `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:24` sets `textStyle: 'price'` in `baseStyle.container`, which is the *same* for PDP and cart. `typography.ts:204-210` resolves it to: | | value | |---|---| | `fontSize` | `fontSizes['2xs']` = **`0.875rem` (14px)** | | `lineHeight` | `lineHeights['2xs']` = **`1.125rem` (18px)** | | `fontWeight` | `fontWeights.medium` = **500** | | `letterSpacing` | `letterSpacings.sm` = **`0`** | | `sale` `gap` | `var(--zimm-scale-xs)` = **`0.5rem` (8px)** | | `sale` `minHeight` | `var(--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs)` = **`1.125rem` (18px)** | | `sale.wasPrice` colour | `text.muted` = `grey[300]` = **`#969696`** (~2.9:1 on white) | | `sale.nowPrice` colour | `status.success` = `green[500]` = **`#2d5a3d`** (~8:1 on white) | **So it does *not* render at "PDP scale" in the sense of being too big — it renders too small.** The base cart price is `` with no `fontSize`, inheriting body size; `theme/index.ts:60` replaces `styles.global` wholesale with `globalStyles`, which sets no `body` `fontSize`, so that inherits the 16px browser root — bold (~700). The new price is **14px / weight 500**. Net effect: **on the same cart page, a discounted line's price is smaller and lighter than a non-discounted line's, and green rather than black**, because the two go through different components. That's the visual finding, and it needs designer input, not a code guess. Also: `wasPrice`'s sub-AA `#969696` was signed off in `zimmProductPrice.css.ts:38-41` as *"a considered call by the FE lead to match the design system"* — scoped to the PDP. This PR silently extends that exception to cart, checkout order summary, confirmation and order history without re-approval, against AGENTS.md's WCAG 2.2 AA target. **Translation ids — yes, a real problem.** `product_view.label.was_price` / `product_view.label.now_price` appear in **0 files** across `translations/` and `overrides/app/static/translations/` (that's my full search scope). So every non-English storefront renders the English `defaultMessage`. Pre-existing on the PDP; this PR newly leaks untranslated "Was"/"Now" into cart, checkout summary, confirmation and order history across da-DK, de-DE, en-AE, en-CA, en-CH, en-GB, en-HK, en-US. Compounding it, the ids sit in the **`product_view.*` namespace**, so a translator working the cart/checkout copy batch will not find them — `translations/` is Tier 2, Integration/SI-owned (`protectedFiles.md`), so a component cannot fix its own namespace after the fact. Two *new* ids in this PR are also at 0 coverage: `order_summary.label.promotion_applied_suffix`, `order_summary.label.shipping_tbd` (by contrast the inherited `order_summary.label.promo_applied` is in 26 files and `tax_tbd` in 8 — which is what proves extraction has run for this namespace and simply hasn't for the new keys). --- ## D. The PDP selection state machine Ground truth established first: - `urlColour` (**head:335**) is purely `URLSearchParams(location.search).get('color')` — no fallback in the value itself. - **head:424-442** is a backfill effect: if `urlColour` is falsy and `product.id === requestedProductId`, it `history.replace`s `?color=`. - Colour swatches are **client-side** — `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx:11` `chakra(RouteLink)` used at `:137`. `` branch at `:109-131` is only taken by SFCC-708 cross-master related swatches.) - The swatch href (**head:1275-1289**) deletes `pid` (`:1280`) and preserves every other param. - **`localSizeValue` has exactly one writer and no reset.** `product-view/index.tsx:466` (declaration), `:1271` (the only `setLocalSizeValue` call). Search scope: all of `overrides/`, all of `e2e/`, and all of `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/` — zero other hits. - The page's own `variant = useVariant(product)` (head:405) reads **URL** variation params, so it stays `undefined` while size lives only in local state — which is why the pid-sync effect at **head:539-549** does *not* fire on a size pick. **The PR's premise ("pid is NEVER written to the URL", head:318-319/449-451/477-478) is correct for a size pick specifically**, though the page *does* own a pid-writer 90 lines below and the comment doesn't say so. **D1 — bare PDP URL, no `?color=`, then pick a size.** *Mostly correct, with one deterministic gap.* This is the **common** entry path, not an edge case: the PLP grid (`productListCardMapper.ts:290` — `buildUrl(productUrlBuilder({id: hit.productId}))`), every recently-viewed surface, and every cart/checkout/wishlist line-item link all produce a bare `/product/`. Only home/PDP Einstein rails (unshadowed base `ProductTile/index.jsx:133-139`) and PDP-internal swatches can supply one. `urlColour` is falsy for the first render(s), then the backfill fires. The size dropdown needs the same `product` data the backfill gates on, so a human click cannot realistically land in the window — **low real risk.** But when `defaultColourValue` resolves falsy (line 438 `return`s), `urlColour` stays `undefined` **forever**: `handleVariationChange` (head:484) then discards *every* size pick, `pricingVariantId` returns `urlPid` (undefined), `selectVariantScopedPriceData` hits `variantScopedPrice.ts:118-119` → `null` → head:1326 `null ?? headerProps.priceData` falls back to master-range pricing. Graceful, not a crash — but Was/Now never narrows to the selected size. Two ways to reach it: a master with **no `color` variation attribute** (size-only), or one where every colour value is explicitly `orderable: false`. **D2 — size M on colour A, switch to colour B.** *Incorrect UI/price disagreement.* No remount → `localSizeValue` stays `'M'` → `effectiveControlledVariationValues` (product-view:468-479) rebuilds as `{color: B, size: 'M'}` → `effectiveSizeValue` = `'M'` → **the dropdown at `:1268` still displays M**. Colour navigation does not call `onVariationChange`, so `selectedSizeSelection` still holds `{colour: 'A', …}`. The guard at head:500 (`'A' === 'B'` → false) correctly zeroes `effectiveSize`; `urlPid` is undefined (swatch deleted it) → colour-range pricing. **Result: the UI claims a specific size is selected while the price silently reverts to colour-range treatment.** The guard does exactly what its comment says — the problem is the UI it's guarding against. **D3 — switch back to colour A without touching the dropdown.** *Correct outcome, fragile mechanism.* `selectedSizeSelection` is `{colour:'A', size:'M', productId}`, never reset (single writer, head:485). Both guards pass → `effectiveSize = 'M'` → `pricingVariantId` = the A/M variant → Was/Now shows, and the dropdown shows M. **UI and price agree.** But this is only correct *because `localSizeValue` is never reset*. If someone fixes that real ProductView bug, `selectedSizeSelection` keeps saying `M` while the dropdown shows nothing selected — a single-variant Was/Now for a size the shopper can't see chosen. **The PR's correctness here is load-bearing on an undocumented bug in another component**, and nothing records that coupling. Same shape on product→product navigation (`path="/product/:productId"`, no remount): the `productId` guard (head:501) correctly rejects the stale size for *pricing*, while the dropdown still shows product A's size on product B. Credit due — that guard is genuinely necessary and correct. **D4 — which `product` does the memo see?** *Correct, for a reason the PR doesn't state.* On a size pick no `pid` is written, so `requestedProductId` stays the master and `product` is the **master** — `variants[]` populated, the `find` at head:505-509 works. Separately, a standalone-variant response *does* carry `variants[]`: base `isVariantValueOrderable` (`use-variation-attributes.js:74-82`) does `product.variants.filter(...)` completely unguarded and is called at `:162` on every render, so the base PDP would throw on every deep-linked variant page otherwise. (`variantScopedPrice.ts:62-64` cites "line 162" for the unguarded access — that's the *call site*; the access is in `isVariantValueOrderable`. Inference from base code, **not** live-API verified.) And when `product` *is* a non-master, `getPriceData` ignores injected variants entirely — `product-utils.js:257` uses `[product]` — so the price comes from the variant's own `tieredPrices`. Fallback is `match?.productId ?? urlPid` (head:510), which can be `undefined` → colour-range → Was/Now suppressed. No crash path. **One unverified edge:** the `find` matches on colour+size only. A master with a **third** variation axis would have multiple matches and `find` silently takes the first, pricing the wrong SKU. Mechanism confirmed in source; I could not confirm whether such a product exists in the catalogue. --- ## Numbered findings **1. `item-price.tsx:104-108` — product name dropped from the price announcement on 8 surfaces.** Mechanism: the new `ZimmProductPrice` branch omits `labelForA11y`, which lines 111 and 118 still pass on both `DisplayPrice` branches. `display-price/current-price.jsx:56-66`'s `VisuallyHidden` node is the *only* construct joining name to price anywhere in the chain; nothing else in base `product-item/index.jsx:54-131` or any of the 8 callers does it (scope stated in §A). Scenario: a screen-reader user tabs a 4-item cart with 2 discounted lines and hears `"Was $795.00 Now $595.00"` twice with nothing saying which garment. Undiscounted lines still announce their name — so it's inconsistent *within one cart*. Severity: **Should-fix** (arguably blocking against AGENTS.md's WCAG 2.2 AA target). Confidence: **high**. **2. `item-price.tsx:107` — `isLive={true}` in a repeated list, against the atom's own documented guidance and an in-repo precedent.** Mechanism: `zimmProductPrice/index.tsx:56-62` documents `isLive={false}` for exactly this case — *"when this atom is reused inside a grid of many cards … where the price never changes after mount"* — and `zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:157` already applies it. Here the price *does* change (order-discount redistribution), so `false` isn't automatically right either — but `true` plus no name (finding 1) is the worst combination. The atom's docblock at `:127-131` justifies having no hidden name node on the premise that *"`currentPrice` arrives already formatted … by the page"* — true on a single-price PDP, false in a list of N. Severity: **Should-fix**. Confidence: **high**. **3. `order-summary/index.tsx:29` — base-path import of a component this same PR overrides; the new story and test silently exercise the base component.** Mechanism: exactly the trap `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` documents under "Importing an already-overridden component from a new component". I verified both halves: `.storybook/main.js:32` aliases `@salesforce/retail-react-app` straight to `node_modules`, and `vitest.config.ts`'s `alias` block has **no** entry for that package. Only the real app build runs `ccExtensibility` (`package.json` → `overridesDir: "overrides"`). Scenario: `index.stories.tsx`'s four stories and `index.test.tsx`'s seven tests render base `item-price.jsx` — no Was/Now, no `ZimmProductPrice`, no live region. Anyone using them to sanity-check discount rendering gets a false negative. Fix: `'../item-variant/item-price'`. The sibling imports (`item-variant`, `item-image`, `item-name`, `item-attributes`, lines 25-28) have no override and are correctly left on the base path. Severity: **Should-fix**. Confidence: **high** (config verified, not just the rule doc). **4. `order-summary/index.tsx:218` and `:368` — `?? 0` fabricates a confident `$0.00` for an unknown total.** Mechanism: `productSubTotal ?? 0` and `orderTotal ?? productTotal ?? 0`. Base had no fallback and rendered `NaN` (react-intl's `formatNumber` try/catches and returns `String(value)` — `@formatjs/intl/lib/src/number.js:36-45`), so this *is* an improvement over a crash-adjacent render, but `$0.00` reads as a real value where `NaN` reads as broken. The same file gets this right two rows away — `:286-313` shows **TBD** for null `shippingTotal`, and `index.stories.tsx:106-107` states the principle explicitly: *"TBD, not a fabricated $0.00."* Applied to shipping and tax, not to subtotal or order total. Against AGENTS.md Graceful Degradation ("surface an explicit error instead"). Severity: **Should-fix**. Confidence: **high**. **5. `product-detail/index.tsx:484` — size selections are silently discarded whenever `urlColour` never resolves.** Mechanism and both trigger conditions in §D1. Not a race (that window is unreachable by a human) — a deterministic gap for size-only masters and all-unorderable-colour masters.
